title: Spectroscopy of phonon-coupled integer and fractional Chern insulators: emergence of polarons and chirality deficit of graviton mode
authors: Min Long, Yuzhu Wang, Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Strong electron-phonon coupling can destabilize both Chern insulators (CIs) and fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) in favor of charge order, but whether the instabilities in CI and FCI share a common microscopic mechanism remains unclear. In this paper, we address this question by studying a flat-band Haldane model coupled to dynamical Holstein phonons at integer and fractional fillings using density-matrix renormalization group with local basis optimization. We find that the low-energy effects of phonons are dominated by their dressing of charge-neutral collective modes. In the CI and FCI, phonons dress excitons and magnetorotons into composite modes that we identify as exciton polarons and magnetoroton polarons, respectively. These modes soften strongly upon approaching the transition, while the momenta of their energy minima anticipate the ordering wave vectors of the charge-ordered phases. The phonon spectrum, in turn, acquires dispersive features inherited from the exciton and magnetoroton modes, providing direct lattice signatures of these neutral excitations. Within the FCI phase, electron-phonon coupling also enhances the opposite-chirality spectral weight of the graviton response, thereby resulting in a chirality deficit. Our results provide a unified excitation-based picture of phonon-driven instabilities in CIs and FCIs and establish lattice dynamics as a probe of their neutral collective modes.
summary: This theoretical work examines how electron-phonon coupling destabilizes Chern and fractional Chern insulators by dressing their low-energy neutral excitations into polarons. The study provides a unified picture showing that lattice dynamics reveal these neutral modes, and it quantifies the resulting chirality deficit in the fractional phase. This establishes lattice vibrations as a key diagnostic tool for understanding topological instabilities in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how strong electron-phonon coupling destabilizes both integer and fractional Chern insulators (CIs and FCIs) towards charge order, and whether a common microscopic mechanism governs these instabilities.
main_result: Phonons primarily dress charge-neutral collective modes (excitons and magnetorotons) into polarons, and this dressing mechanism provides a unified picture of the instability, while also causing a measurable chirality deficit in the FCI.
method: The study employs advanced theoretical techniques including Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) with Local Basis Optimization (LBO) and Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP) to analyze spectral functions and gap evolution.
model_or_system:
The system is modeled using a flat-band Haldane model coupled to dynamical Holstein phonons, analyzed at integer and fractional fillings ($
u$). The analysis extends to probing the chiral response via quadrupolar operators.
key_observables: Exciton and magnetoroton polarons, phonon spectral function, charge order parameters ($M(\mathbf{k}), S(\mathbf{k})$), and the chirality deficit of the graviton mode.
important_parameters:
Electron-phonon coupling strength ($g$), filling fraction ($
u$), and the relative gap sizes ($\Delta_c, \Delta_n, \Delta_{ph}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that phonon effects are dominated by dressing charge-neutral modes, and in some parts, approximations like the static limit or Gaussian coupling profiles are used.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the formation of exciton and magnetoroton polarons, the evolution of charge order parameters across phase transitions, and the quantitative measurement of the chirality deficit in the FCI.
paper_structure: The paper develops a unified excitation-based picture, first detailing the polaron formation in CIs and FCIs, then quantifying the resulting chirality deficit in the FCI, and finally establishing lattice dynamics as a direct probe for these neutral excitations.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between lattice dynamics (phonons) and topological electronic states (CIs/FCIs) via polaron formation is highly relevant for understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated quantum materials.
